matchstick.title: Transform V into X by repositioning one stick
matchstick.principle: If a V (two diagonal sticks) appears, moving one of its sticks so that it crosses the other converts it into an X, changing the numeral’s value from 5 to 10. Skipping this intra‑character move can miss a simple way to balance the equation.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever a V is present and the equality is off by roughly 5, try converting the V to X before considering inter‑character moves.
matchstick.example: A rejected attempt kept the V unchanged and only tried moving sticks between characters, missing the V→X conversion that could have fixed the equation.

matchstick.title: Move a vertical I‑stick between numerals
matchstick.principle: A vertical stick representing an I can be detached from any numeral containing I’s and attached to another numeral (or placed as a new I) without breaking the source or target symbols. This often adjusts a value by ±1 and can resolve near‑miss equalities.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation is off by a small amount (1 or 2) and there is an I somewhere that can be moved without destroying its original numeral.
matchstick.example: In a rejected attempt, the solver never tried moving the I from the left side to the right side, missing the chance to increase the RHS by 1.

matchstick.title: Prefer intra‑character stick relocation
matchstick.principle: First explore moving a stick within the same character (e.g., turning V→X, X→V, I↔L) because such changes keep the overall stick count and often yield a valid numeral with minimal impact. Ignoring intra‑character moves can waste effort on more complex inter‑character relocations.
matchstick.when_to_apply: At the start of the search, before trying to move sticks between different symbols.
matchstick.example: A rejected attempt immediately considered moving sticks between characters, overlooking the possibility of converting X to V within the same character.

matchstick.title: Validate source and target symbols after a stick move
matchstick.principle: After detaching a stick, both the originating symbol and the destination symbol must still correspond to a valid Roman numeral or operator; otherwise the move is illegal. Failing to check this leads to invalid intermediate symbols.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After each hypothetical stick relocation, before evaluating the arithmetic.
matchstick.example: An attempt removed a diagonal from an X, leaving a single diagonal, which is not a valid numeral, but the solver proceeded to evaluate the equation.

matchstick.title: Avoid creating single angled sticks (invalid numerals)
matchstick.principle: A lone diagonal stick does not represent any Roman numeral; V and X require two diagonals. Ensure that any move does not leave a single diagonal isolated.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever a diagonal stick is removed from a V or X, verify that the remaining shape still forms a valid numeral.
matchstick.example: A rejected attempt tried to take a diagonal from an X without adding another diagonal, producing an invalid symbol.

matchstick.title: Convert + to - by moving its vertical stick
matchstick.principle: A plus sign consists of a vertical and a horizontal stick; removing the vertical stick turns it into a minus sign, and the removed stick can be reused elsewhere. This operator change often balances the equation with a single move.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation contains a plus sign and the equality is off by a value that could be corrected by switching addition to subtraction.
matchstick.example: In a rejected attempt, the solver never considered turning the + into –, missing the solution IX = XIII – IV.

matchstick.title: Create a new numeral by moving a stick to a new position (reordering)
matchstick.principle: A detached stick can be placed as a separate character, forming a new numeral (e.g., adding a vertical stick to create an I). This can increase or decrease the total value without altering existing symbols.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation is off by a whole numeral and there is a spare stick that can become a new I or V.
matchstick.example: A rejected attempt never tried using a removed stick to create a brand‑new I on the right side.

matchstick.title: Consider inter‑character stick relocation when intra‑character moves fail
matchstick.principle: If no intra‑character relocation yields a valid equality, then explore moving a stick from one character to another, ensuring both remain valid. This expands the search space systematically.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After exhausting all intra‑character possibilities without success.
matchstick.example: A rejected attempt jumped straight to inter‑character moves without first checking all intra‑character options like X→V.

matchstick.title: Swap operators via horizontal stick move
matchstick.principle: The equals sign (=) consists of two horizontal sticks; moving one to a minus sign (-) turns the equals into a minus and the minus into an equals. This operator swap can dramatically change the equation’s structure with a single stick.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation contains both = and - (or +) and a simple operator swap might balance the arithmetic.
matchstick.example: A rejected attempt performed the swap but did not verify the resulting arithmetic, leading to an incorrect equality.

matchstick.title: Transform X into V by repositioning one diagonal stick within the same character
matchstick.principle: An X is made of two crossing diagonals; moving one diagonal so that the two diagonals meet at a point (instead of crossing) converts the X into a V, reducing its value from 10 to 5. This intra‑character change can adjust the total by 5 and should be tried before more complex moves.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever an X appears and the equality is off by roughly 5, try converting that X to a V by moving one diagonal within the character.
matchstick.example: In the failed attempts for matchstick_006, the solver never considered turning an X into a V, missing a potential 5‑point adjustment.

matchstick.description: Overlooking intra‑character transformations (e.g., X→V) before inter‑character moves
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model tends to focus on moving sticks between symbols, ignoring the simpler possibility of reshaping a symbol itself.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Systematically enumerate all intra‑character stick relocations (including X→V, V→X, I↔L) before exploring inter‑character moves.

matchstick.description: Assuming sticks retain their orientation and not rotating horizontals to verticals (or vice versa) when repositioning
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model treats horizontal and vertical sticks as distinct types, missing that a horizontal can be placed vertically to form an I.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Remember that a stick can be reoriented arbitrarily; consider rotating a horizontal stick to vertical when creating a new I or L.

matchstick.description: Not evaluating the arithmetic result after each candidate transformation
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model sometimes jumps to conclusions about validity without checking the numeric equality.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After any hypothetical move, compute the Roman numeral values and verify the equality before accepting the transformation.

matchstick.description: Assuming operator swaps (e.g., = ↔ -) automatically solve the puzzle
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model treats operator swapping as a generic fix without checking if the new arithmetic holds.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always recalculate the expression after swapping operators to confirm it yields a true equality.

matchstick.description: Ignoring the I↔L transformation (adding/removing a horizontal stick to/from an I)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model does not consider that an I can become an L by adding a horizontal, which changes its value from 1 to 50.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Include I↔L as a possible intra‑character move when the equation is off by a large amount (e.g., 49).
